shortDescription: Poland's manufacturing downturn eased in September as output, new orders and employment all fell at slower rates, a business survey showed on Thursday.

children: Poland's manufacturing downturn eased in September as output, new orders and employment all fell at slower rates, a business survey showed on Thursday.
The S&P Global Poland Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to 49.0 in September from 48.3 in August, a survey by S&P Global showed. The 50-mark separates growth from contraction.
Analysts polled by Reuters had expected a reading of 48.9.

"(A) number of key metrics moved in the right direction as output, new orders and employment all fell more slowly than in August," said Trevor Balchin, Economics Director at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

New orders fell for an 18th straight month, though the rate of decline moderated from August. Export demand remained weak, with new export orders dropping for a 10th month and at the fastest pace in three months.
Manufacturers cut jobs only marginally. Employment fell for the 16th time in 17 months.

Cost pressures eased for the fourth time in five months, although input price inflation remained above the long-run average. Output price inflation strengthened slightly in September, while suppliers' delivery times lengthened again and input stocks rose for a second month.
